In one or two sentences: the claim is **false**. The round-trip-efficiency sub-claim fails on a hard physical-law basis — a Carnot ceiling of ≈62-64% at these temperatures against ambient, with real documented practice around 33-40%, both far below 85% — and the cost-competitiveness sub-claim fails independently, since a 5 MWh unit's power-block fixed-cost floor puts its effective delivered-electricity cost roughly 5-85× above utility lithium-ion. Overall confidence is LOW (driven by several unverified/estimated inputs in the cost analysis), but the efficiency falsification alone rests on an unsuffixed physical law and holds regardless of that caveat.
